notes: I changed the x<=0 branch from `floor(x)-1` to `ceil(x)-1`. E3 revealed that negative non-integers map to floor(x) (e.g. f(-0.5)=-1, f(-127.5)=-128), which is ceil(x)-1, while integer negatives still give x-1 (also ceil(x)-1). The old floor(x)-1 over-subtracted by 1 at every non-integer negative point.
